title: Finals Exam Reviewer
description: Chapters 9–11: Developing Future Architecture Views, Developing an EA Management Plan, and the Role of Investment Planning and Project Management. Multiple choice + True or False.

questions.explanation: Chapter 9 - Developing Future Architecture Views

options: An integrated narrative and set of planning assumptions
A network connectivity diagram and an equipment inventory
A data dictionary of entities and formats
A list of hardware and software products

questions.question: High-level resource planning supported by IT-related strategic initiatives is also known as the:
options: Capital planning and investment control (CPIC) process
Systems analysis and design method (SADM) process

questions.explanation: Chapter 9 - Developing Future Architecture Views

options: Outsourcing of an existing process to a vendor
Minor improvement of an existing process
Major reengineering of an existing process
Introduction of a completely new process
questions.explanation: Chapter 9 - Developing Future Architecture Views. The four types: new process, elimination, major reengineering, and minor improvement.

questions.question: Reviews of existing business services, to find those that are obsolete or duplicative, should be performed periodically by:
questions.explanation: Chapter 9 - Developing Future Architecture Views

questions.question: Documenting approved changes to business services helps maintain this kind of alignment with strategic goals and initiatives.

questions.explanation: Chapter 9 - Developing Future Architecture Views

questions.question: A future view of a PMP may NOT be needed with methods that develop the entire system capability in one effort, such as:
questions.explanation: Chapter 9 - Developing Future Architecture Views

questions.question: Which is an example where having both a current and future view of the PMP would be beneficial?
options: A waterfall project where the whole system is delivered in one release
Phased implementation of large ERP projects with several modules
A small website developed in a single effort
A one-time purchase of desktop computers

questions.question: The part of the PMP that documents the value of the investment to the enterprise.

questions.explanation: Chapter 9 - Developing Future Architecture Views

options: Objects can be modified with minimal effort to reflect changes in requirements
OO removes the need for logical and physical data models in system design
OO only works with proprietary products from one vendor
Objects never need to be changed once they are created

questions.explanation: Chapter 9 - Developing Future Architecture Views

questions.explanation: Chapter 9 - Developing Future Architecture Views

questions.explanation: Chapter 9 - Developing Future Architecture Views

questions.question: WSDL descriptions of web services are kept in the:
questions.explanation: Chapter 9 - Developing Future Architecture Views

questions.explanation: Chapter 9 - Developing Future Architecture Views

questions.question: Network technical standards in the future view include changes reflected in models such as:
options: The OSI model and TCP/IP model
questions.explanation: Chapter 9 - Developing Future Architecture Views

questions.question: Future views of security documentation include the related security documentation for applications and databases, and the:
questions.explanation: Chapter 9 - Developing Future Architecture Views

questions.question: The future view of EACRs consists of an archive of:
options: Rejected EA Change Requests from previous years
Approved, but yet to be implemented EA Change Requests
Completed projects and their post-implementation reviews
questions.explanation: Chapter 9 - Developing Future Architecture Views

questions.question: What is a Concept of Operations (CONOPS) scenario?
options: A narrative of the current or a plausible future operating environment
A list of approved EA Change Requests yet to be implemented
A diagram of the network cables and racks in the data center
A table that lists the roles and duties of the EA team members
questions.explanation: Chapter 9 - Developing Future Architecture Views

questions.question: What is the Project Management Plan (PMP)?
options: A one-time report written after a project is closed and archived
A registry where web service descriptions are kept for clients
A living document with standardized ways to implement IT resources
A budget table that lists only the hardware costs of the EA
questions.explanation: Chapter 9 - Developing Future Architecture Views

questions.question: What is the "as-is" view of the EA?
options: The future view, documenting resources years from now
The list of initiatives without executive sponsorship
The archive of change requests yet to be implemented
The current view, documenting IT resources active today
questions.explanation: Chapter 9 - Developing Future Architecture Views

questions.question: The future view of the EA is also known as the "as-is" view.
questions.explanation: Chapter 9 - Developing Future Architecture Views. The future view is the "to-be" view; the "as-is" view documents current IT resources.

questions.question: Future EA views provide an authoritative reference for discussing options and changes during development.
questions.explanation: Chapter 9 - Developing Future Architecture Views

questions.question: Initiatives in the very early stages of consideration should always be included in future EA views.
questions.explanation: Chapter 9 - Developing Future Architecture Views. They can be left out until they have firm sponsor backing, strong business cases, and viable technical solutions.

questions.question: Cluttering future EA views with initiatives that have little chance of being implemented can detract from the perceived value of the EA.
questions.explanation: Chapter 9 - Developing Future Architecture Views

questions.question: CONOPS scenarios looking into the future have mainly been used as a financial accounting tool.
questions.explanation: Chapter 9 - Developing Future Architecture Views. They have been used as a military planning tool for millennia.

questions.question: CONOPS scenarios document both the current operating environment and a number of plausible future operating environments.
questions.explanation: Chapter 9 - Developing Future Architecture Views

questions.question: It is possible to predict exactly which internal and external factors will create a helpful or hostile operating environment.
questions.explanation: Chapter 9 - Developing Future Architecture Views. It is impossible to predict, which is why several future scenarios are helpful.

questions.question: The future view of strategic plans can serve as draft documents where potential changes that have executive sponsorship are recorded.
questions.explanation: Chapter 9 - Developing Future Architecture Views

questions.question: Strategic scenarios can be added or deleted from the Strategic Plan's future view in response to changes in the operating environment.
questions.explanation: Chapter 9 - Developing Future Architecture Views

questions.question: Updated strategic plans should be published every month.
questions.explanation: Chapter 9 - Developing Future Architecture Views. Updated plans should be published every few years.

questions.question: New strategic goals serve to direct the development of future operating scenarios.
questions.explanation: Chapter 9 - Developing Future Architecture Views

questions.question: There are six general types of changes to business services.
questions.explanation: Chapter 9 - Developing Future Architecture Views. There are four: new process, elimination, major reengineering, and minor improvement.

questions.question: At the Business Level, all potential changes to business services should be documented, even those without executive sponsorship.
questions.explanation: Chapter 9 - Developing Future Architecture Views. Only potential changes that have executive sponsorship should be documented.

questions.question: Downward alignment ensures that EA components and artifacts at the lower three levels are adjusted to support anticipated process changes.
questions.explanation: Chapter 9 - Developing Future Architecture Views

questions.question: PMPs are maintained on systems throughout the lifecycle, until the system is disposed.
questions.explanation: Chapter 9 - Developing Future Architecture Views

questions.question: The investment business case usually requires a review at least annually.
questions.explanation: Chapter 9 - Developing Future Architecture Views

questions.question: If an investment no longer generates sufficient benefits, it should be cancelled or modified.
questions.explanation: Chapter 9 - Developing Future Architecture Views

questions.question: Object reuse increases the cost of systems upgrade projects.
questions.explanation: Chapter 9 - Developing Future Architecture Views. Object reuse lowers the cost of systems upgrade projects.

questions.question: Data Dictionaries store the actual data of the enterprise's IT systems.
questions.explanation: Chapter 9 - Developing Future Architecture Views. Data Dictionaries do not store actual data; they list entities, attributes, data field formats, and standards.

questions.question: Various versions of an object can be separately stored for use in different systems and applications.
questions.explanation: Chapter 9 - Developing Future Architecture Views

questions.question: APIs can never include open standards.
questions.explanation: Chapter 9 - Developing Future Architecture Views. APIs may include open standards if maximum integration is desired, or be proprietary and limit interoperability.

questions.question: The same documentation techniques should be used for current and future views so that changes are easier to highlight and compare.
questions.explanation: Chapter 9 - Developing Future Architecture Views

questions.question: The document that describes how an enterprise will manage the transition of its current processes and resources to those that will be needed in the future.
questions.explanation: Chapter 10 - Developing an EA Management Plan

questions.question: The transition from the current EA to the future EA is:
options: An ongoing activity, as new resources are implemented and become part of the current EA
Not part of EA management, since it belongs only to project management and the PMP
Handled only by the webmaster when the EA website is updated
A one-time event that is completed within a single fiscal year
questions.explanation: Chapter 10 - Developing an EA Management Plan

questions.question: The EA Management Plan is updated at regular intervals (e.g., annually) to provide:
options: New hardware and software purchases for every department and office
Clear version control for changes in current and future views
A completely new EA framework for each year
Daily status reports for every ongoing project
questions.explanation: Chapter 10 - Developing an EA Management Plan

questions.question: Where should the EA Management Plan be archived?
questions.explanation: Chapter 10 - Developing an EA Management Plan

questions.question: Which part of the EA Management Plan contains Governance and Principles, EA Roles and Responsibilities, and the EA Program Budget?
questions.explanation: Chapter 10 - Developing an EA Management Plan

questions.question: Which part of the EA Management Plan contains Future Operating Scenarios, Planning Assumptions, and the Sequencing Plan?
questions.explanation: Chapter 10 - Developing an EA Management Plan

questions.question: EA governance is best described through a narrative that provides EA program policy and an accompanying:
options: Cable plant diagram of each building
Data dictionary of all EA entities
Flow chart that shows how and when decisions are made
Rack elevation diagram of the enterprise network center
questions.explanation: Chapter 10 - Developing an EA Management Plan

questions.question: These articulate the enterprise's values as they relate to the EA and guide the EA program's establishment and management.
questions.explanation: Chapter 10 - Developing an EA Management Plan

questions.question: Which is an example of an EA principle?
options: The recognition that IT is normally a means and not an end in itself
Only proprietary products should be used
IT should always be purchased first, before a business case is written
Stakeholders should not participate in EA
questions.explanation: Chapter 10 - Developing an EA Management Plan

questions.question: For EA to be viewed as part of the strategic planning process, business executives must:
options: See the value of the EA program in supporting the outcomes that matter to them
Manage the EA repository and the EA software application
Write all of the EA documentation themselves at every level
Personally approve every hardware and software purchase in the enterprise
questions.explanation: Chapter 10 - Developing an EA Management Plan

questions.explanation: Chapter 10 - Developing an EA Management Plan

questions.explanation: Chapter 10 - Developing an EA Management Plan

questions.question: EA team position that facilitates the establishment of the EA program, leads the resolution of high-level issues, and integrates EA and other governance.
questions.explanation: Chapter 10 - Developing an EA Management Plan

questions.question: EA team position that manages the EA program, selects the EA framework, identifies EA standards, and manages the EA configuration management sub-process.
questions.explanation: Chapter 10 - Developing an EA Management Plan

questions.question: EA team position responsible for maintenance of the EA software application and the EA repository.
questions.explanation: Chapter 10 - Developing an EA Management Plan

questions.question: EA team position that provides technical analysis and design support for database-related EA components.
questions.explanation: Chapter 10 - Developing an EA Management Plan

questions.question: EA team position whose role is Requirements Identification / QA, identifying end-user requirements and giving feedback on solutions.
questions.explanation: Chapter 10 - Developing an EA Management Plan

questions.question: The EA program budget is documented by fiscal year and over the total lifecycle so that this is identified.
questions.explanation: Chapter 10 - Developing an EA Management Plan

questions.question: The initial estimate of EA program costs represents the:
options: Final cost of the EA program
questions.explanation: Chapter 10 - Developing an EA Management Plan

questions.question: These measures identify progress being made toward some new end-state, such as better EA component integration.
questions.explanation: Chapter 10 - Developing an EA Management Plan

questions.question: These measures provide data on activities and things, such as how many databases exist.
questions.explanation: Chapter 10 - Developing an EA Management Plan

questions.question: "Reduce IT project planning average costs by ten percent within one year" is an example of a(n):
questions.explanation: Chapter 10 - Developing an EA Management Plan

questions.question: Part 2 of the EA Management Plan helps the present role of IT to be analyzed from either a:
questions.explanation: Chapter 10 - Developing an EA Management Plan

questions.question: EA components should not be procured unless:
options: Every end user has requested the same component
The component replaces all existing systems at once
The vendor offers the lowest price for the component
There is a strong business case that supports investment
questions.explanation: Chapter 10 - Developing an EA Management Plan

questions.question: When documenting current systems and applications, comments should focus on degree of integration, potential scalability, user satisfaction, and:
options: The age of every server in the data center
The color scheme of each user interface
The number of programmers on each team
questions.explanation: Chapter 10 - Developing an EA Management Plan

questions.question: The current infrastructure is evaluated on how well internal and external networks, systems, and cable plants integrate to create a:
questions.explanation: Chapter 10 - Developing an EA Management Plan

questions.question: Why should specific IT security information NOT be part of the EA Management Plan?
options: It is too expensive to print
Security is not part of EA
questions.explanation: Chapter 10 - Developing an EA Management Plan

questions.question: The standards section documents this, which provides EA standards for voice, data, video, and IT security.
questions.explanation: Chapter 10 - Developing an EA Management Plan

questions.question: The most valuable resource an enterprise often has is its:
questions.explanation: Chapter 10 - Developing an EA Management Plan

questions.question: In the EA3 framework, updates to current and future views should be accomplished in this manner to preserve the emphasis on strategy and business.
questions.explanation: Chapter 10 - Developing an EA Management Plan. Updates begin with the enterprise's strategic goals and initiatives.

questions.question: This section documents the tasks, milestones, and timeframe for implementing new EA components and artifacts.
questions.explanation: Chapter 10 - Developing an EA Management Plan

questions.question: This section supports the sub-process by which changes to the EA are managed and the standards in the TSRM are applied.
questions.explanation: Chapter 10 - Developing an EA Management Plan

questions.question: Configuration management ensures that waivers have specific time limits so that:
questions.explanation: Chapter 10 - Developing an EA Management Plan

questions.question: Part 4 of the EA Management Plan provides a Glossary of EA terms along with a(n):
questions.explanation: Chapter 10 - Developing an EA Management Plan. Because EA is still an emerging area of practice, these create a common set of terms.

questions.question: What is EA governance?
options: The decision process for EA issues like investments and standards
The hardware and network that support the EA repository
The software application used to store the EA documentation
The glossary and acronym list at the end of the EA Plan
questions.explanation: Chapter 10 - Developing an EA Management Plan

questions.question: What are EA principles?
options: Diagrams that show the current network infrastructure
Technical standards for voice, data, and video systems
Statements of the enterprise's values that guide the EA program
Fiscal year budgets for each part of the EA program
questions.explanation: Chapter 10 - Developing an EA Management Plan

questions.question: What is a waiver in EA configuration management?
options: A request to add a new component to the EA
A permanent exception that removes a standard for good
A budget approval for the EA program each year
A time-limited permission not to follow an EA standard
questions.explanation: Chapter 10 - Developing an EA Management Plan

questions.question: The EA Management Plan documents the enterprise's performance gaps, resource requirements, planned solutions, a sequencing plan, and a summary of the current and future architecture.
questions.explanation: Chapter 10 - Developing an EA Management Plan

questions.question: The EA Management Plan is a one-time document that is never updated.
questions.explanation: Chapter 10 - Developing an EA Management Plan. It is a living document updated at regular intervals (e.g., annually).

questions.question: Large and mid-size enterprises often have many IT projects underway at any given time, which requires coordination, prioritization, and oversight.
questions.explanation: Chapter 10 - Developing an EA Management Plan

questions.question: The EA Management Plan has four parts.
questions.explanation: Chapter 10 - Developing an EA Management Plan. Program Management, Current Architecture Summary, Future Architecture Summary, Glossary and References.

questions.question: An emphasis on using commercial products that are based on open standards is an example of an EA principle.
questions.explanation: Chapter 10 - Developing an EA Management Plan

questions.question: The Webmaster is responsible for selecting and implementing the EA framework and documentation methodology.
questions.explanation: Chapter 10 - Developing an EA Management Plan. That is the Chief Architect's responsibility; the Webmaster maintains the EA website.

questions.question: The EA Tool Expert participates in EA program decision-making and promotes the identification of IT-related requirements for each LOB.
questions.explanation: Chapter 10 - Developing an EA Management Plan. That describes Line of Business Managers; the EA Tool Expert maintains the EA software application and repository.

questions.question: If the scope of the EA program changes, a corresponding change in the funding baseline should also be made.
questions.explanation: Chapter 10 - Developing an EA Management Plan

questions.question: Output measures often have both quantitative and qualitative elements, while outcome measures are usually quantitative.
questions.explanation: Chapter 10 - Developing an EA Management Plan. It is the reverse: outcome measures have both elements; output measures are usually quantitative.

questions.question: The attainment of outcomes correlates to goal attainment, which is the most important thing to an enterprise.
questions.explanation: Chapter 10 - Developing an EA Management Plan

questions.question: "Number of IT projects planned that year" is an example of an output measure.
questions.explanation: Chapter 10 - Developing an EA Management Plan

questions.question: Part 2 of the EA Management Plan should duplicate all of the extensive documentation of the current EA.
questions.explanation: Chapter 10 - Developing an EA Management Plan. Its objective is not to duplicate it, but to give an integrated view of how components and artifacts support each other.

questions.question: IT security should be part of any strategic goal or initiative that depends on accurate, properly authenticated information.
questions.explanation: Chapter 10 - Developing an EA Management Plan

questions.question: Updates to the current and future views of the EA should begin with the technology infrastructure.
questions.explanation: Chapter 10 - Developing an EA Management Plan. Updates are done top-down, beginning with the strategic goals and initiatives.

questions.question: Changes to the EA include the addition, upgrade, and retirement of EA components or artifacts.
questions.explanation: Chapter 10 - Developing an EA Management Plan

questions.question: Configuration management allows waivers with no time limits.
questions.explanation: Chapter 10 - Developing an EA Management Plan. Waivers have specific time limits so that EA standards are eventually realized.

questions.question: A bibliographical list of reference books and articles is included in Part 4 of the EA Management Plan.
questions.explanation: Chapter 10 - Developing an EA Management Plan

questions.question: The management and decision-making process associated with the planning, selection, control, and evaluation of investments in resources, including EA components.
questions.explanation: Chapter 11 - The Role of Investment Planning and Project Management

questions.question: What are the four phases of the CPIC process?
questions.explanation: Chapter 11 - The Role of Investment Planning and Project Management

questions.question: The EA program is only effective if the enterprise's resources are effectively applied to:
questions.explanation: Chapter 11 - The Role of Investment Planning and Project Management. If there were no gaps, there would be no requirement for new or upgraded EA components.

questions.question: Which of the following is promoted by the CPIC process?
options: Approving every proposed investment regardless of its value
Avoiding business cases so that investments can be approved faster
Ignoring operational performance gaps until projects are completed
Encouraging a culture of learning by evaluating each completed investment
questions.explanation: Chapter 11 - The Role of Investment Planning and Project Management

questions.question: In which CPIC phase are requirements, the business case, and the project plan developed?
questions.explanation: Chapter 11 - The Role of Investment Planning and Project Management

questions.question: The CPIC phase where a funding decision is made for a proposed investment in an EA component.
questions.explanation: Chapter 11 - The Role of Investment Planning and Project Management

questions.question: The CPIC phase where ongoing projects are evaluated for how closely cost, schedule, and performance milestones are being met, and how well risk is managed.
questions.explanation: Chapter 11 - The Role of Investment Planning and Project Management

questions.question: The CPIC phase where completed IT projects receive a Post-Implementation Review (PIR) and operational systems are reviewed for continuing value.
questions.explanation: Chapter 11 - The Role of Investment Planning and Project Management

questions.question: In the CPIC process, which document is at the center, connecting all four phases?
questions.explanation: Chapter 11 - The Role of Investment Planning and Project Management

questions.question: Governance processes, including CPIC, should be overseen by a(n):
options: External vendor that supplies the enterprise's ERP solution
Executive Steering Committee comprised of the enterprise's top executives
Webmaster and research analyst of the EA team
Group of end-user representatives chosen from each line of business
questions.explanation: Chapter 11 - The Role of Investment Planning and Project Management

questions.question: Project and Program Managers control successful outcomes by managing five primary aspects. Which of the following is one of them?
questions.explanation: Chapter 11 - The Role of Investment Planning and Project Management. The five: managing scope, controlling costs, maintaining the schedule, achieving product performance, mitigating risk.

questions.question: A temporary endeavor undertaken to create a unique product, service, or result.
questions.explanation: Chapter 11 - The Role of Investment Planning and Project Management

questions.question: An ongoing endeavor that manages existing processes/resources, or oversees the development of new processes/resources via projects.
questions.explanation: Chapter 11 - The Role of Investment Planning and Project Management

questions.question: In the Project Management Plan outline, Alternatives Analysis, Cost-Benefit Analysis, and Return on Investment Analysis are part of the:
questions.explanation: Chapter 11 - The Role of Investment Planning and Project Management

questions.question: In the Project Management Plan outline, the Schedule and Work Breakdown Structure and Risk Management are part of:
questions.explanation: Chapter 11 - The Role of Investment Planning and Project Management

questions.question: What is a Post-Implementation Review (PIR)?
options: A business case written in the CPIC Planning Phase
A funding decision made in the CPIC Selection Phase
A review of a completed IT project in the CPIC Evaluation Phase
A check of cost and schedule in the CPIC Control Phase
questions.explanation: Chapter 11 - The Role of Investment Planning and Project Management

questions.question: What is CPIC?
questions.explanation: Chapter 11 - The Role of Investment Planning and Project Management

questions.question: The CPIC process is a cyclic process.
questions.explanation: Chapter 11 - The Role of Investment Planning and Project Management

questions.question: If there were no gaps in operational performance, there would still be a requirement for new or upgraded EA components.
questions.explanation: Chapter 11 - The Role of Investment Planning and Project Management. If there were no gaps, there would be no requirement for new or upgraded EA components.

questions.question: A significant part of IT governance is implemented through the CPIC process.
questions.explanation: Chapter 11 - The Role of Investment Planning and Project Management

questions.question: In the CPIC Selection Phase, completed IT projects receive a Post-Implementation Review.
questions.explanation: Chapter 11 - The Role of Investment Planning and Project Management. The PIR happens in the Evaluation Phase; the Selection Phase makes the funding decision.

questions.question: Project management focuses on developing, implementing, operating, improving, and/or retiring enterprise resources.
questions.explanation: Chapter 11 - The Role of Investment Planning and Project Management

questions.question: A program is a temporary endeavor, while a project is an ongoing endeavor.
questions.explanation: Chapter 11 - The Role of Investment Planning and Project Management. A project is temporary; a program is ongoing.

questions.question: The Project Management Plan includes a Security and Privacy section.
questions.explanation: Chapter 11 - The Role of Investment Planning and Project Management
